shots.say: How does your heart work? What makes that thump, thump?
Thump, thump! Your heart beats inside your chest.
shots.tag: hook: the heart in the chest

shots.say: Hi! I'm Gizmo. Let's find out how your heart works!
Gizmo Explains!
Welcome to my lab, body explorers!
I am a robot, so I have no heart. But you do!
Your heart is in your chest, a little to the left of the middle.
Put your hand on your chest. Can you feel a beat?
Where is your heart? In your chest, or in your foot?
In your chest! Your heart is really a muscle.
Is your heart a muscle, or a balloon?
A muscle! It squeezes, and pumps blood around your body.
Make a fist. Squeeze it, and open it, like a heart pumping!
Look at your fist. Your heart is about the size of your fist!
Hold up your fist, and look. That is about how big your heart is!
How big is your heart? As big as your fist, or as big as a car?
Your heart pumps all day, and all night, all the time!
Even when you sleep at night, your heart keeps pumping.
Your heart keeps on going, nice and calm.
Sitting, walking, or playing, your heart is always working!
When does your heart pump? Only in the day, or all the time?
Say it with me. My heart is a muscle!
A muscle, as big as your fist, pumping all the time!
What does your heart pump around your body? Blood!
Blood gives your body oxygen, and good things from your food.
It carries oxygen to every part of you, from your head to your toes!
Touch your head, and then touch your toes!
What does blood carry? Oxygen, or sand?
Oxygen is in the air. Breathe in slowly, and breathe out.
Your heart sends blood to your lungs.
There, the blood picks up oxygen!
Where does blood pick up oxygen? In your lungs, or in your toes?
The lungs! Then your heart pumps the blood all around your body.
Tubes called blood vessels carry it away, and bring it back!
Does the blood come back to your heart? Yes, or no?
Yes! Away and back, over and over again.
Draw a big circle in the air with your finger!
Say it with me. My heart pumps blood!
Where does blood get oxygen? In your lungs, or in your hair?
The lungs! Then the heart sends it all around, and back again.
Listen to a heartbeat. It sounds like lub, dub!
Clap with me, like a heartbeat. Lub, dub! Lub, dub!
Inside your heart are little doors, called valves.
When the doors close, they make the sound. Lub, dub!
What makes the heartbeat sound? Little doors closing, or a tiny drum?
Your heart has four rooms. Two on top, and two on the bottom!
How many rooms are in your heart? Two, or four?
Four! Let's count them. One, two, three, four!
Listen again. Lub, dub, lub, dub. Your heart never stops!
When you run and play, your heart pumps faster!
Why? So your muscles get more oxygen, and can work harder.
Can you march in place? Left, right, left, right!
Let's hop five times! One, two, three, four, five!
Now, hand on your chest. Is your heart beating faster?
When you run and play, does your heart beat faster, or slower?
Running and swimming help keep your heart healthy!
Say it with me. Lub, dub! My heart works hard!
Quiz time! Let's remember what we learned.
How big is your heart? As big as your fist, or as big as a bus?
Your fist! A strong muscle, pumping all the time.
Where does blood pick up oxygen? In your lungs, or in your ears?
In your lungs! Fresh oxygen for your blood.
What makes the lub, dub sound? Little doors, or little bells?
Little doors inside your heart, closing. Lub, dub!
Muscle, blood, oxygen, lub, dub! Thanks for exploring with me!
Gizmo Explains!
